Wine Tours Sedona & Verde Valley: Your Arizona Wine Country Guide

A private Verde Valley wine tour from Phoenix or Scottsdale runs 8 to 12 hours. In our 14-seat Executive Sprinter an 8-hour day bills 7 hours at $145 per hour, or $1,015, about $73 per person for a full van. Nobody drives, everybody tastes, and the cases ride home in the back.

Yes, Arizona makes wine. Good wine. The Verde Valley, just south of Sedona, has become one of the country's most interesting wine regions: high desert elevation, big day-to-night temperature swings, and volcanic soils produce bold, complex wines. And it is an easy run north of Phoenix.

Arizona Wine Country Overview

Why the Verde Valley?

  • Elevation: 3,300-4,500 feet, similar to famous Spanish regions
  • Wineries: dozens in the corridor between Cottonwood, Cornville, Jerome, and Sedona
  • Climate: hot days and cool nights balance sugar and acid in the grapes
  • Soil: ancient volcanic ash and limestone

What to Expect

  • Bolder reds: Rhône varietals such as Syrah, Grenache, and Mourvèdre lead
  • Interesting whites: Viognier, Malvasia, Picpoul Blanc
  • Unique terroir: minerality, dried herbs, subtle smoke
  • Small production: many wineries make only a few thousand cases a year
  • Passionate winemakers: everyone has a story

Top Verde Valley Wineries

Page Springs Cellars — The Pioneer

Page Springs, off 89A. Traditional, minimal-intervention winemaking. Try the Petite Sirah and GSM blends. A rustic tasting room on Oak Creek with cheese and charcuterie. This is the winery that put Arizona on the map.

Javelina Leap Vineyard & Winery — The View

Cornville hilltop. Fruit-forward, approachable wines; try the Zinfandel and Syrah. Family-friendly patio with panoramic valley views and weekend food trucks. Great for groups.

Alcantara Vineyards — The Venue

Near Camp Verde. Italian varietals and Mediterranean blends; try the Sangiovese. Tuscan-estate grounds and a full restaurant. The region's most popular wedding venue.

Burning Tree Cellars — The Boutique

Cornville. Small-batch, terroir-focused; try the Viognier and Grenache. Intimate, educational, and you often meet the winemaker.

Pillsbury Wine Company — The Artist

Cottonwood Main Street. Creative and personality-driven; try the Roan Red and Picpoul Blanc. Sam Pillsbury is a filmmaker-turned-winemaker with stories to match.

Oak Creek Vineyards & Winery — The Classic

Cornville. Traditional varietals and crowd-pleasers; try the Chardonnay and Meritage blends. Relaxed, shaded patio. Ideal for wine newcomers.

Merkin Vineyards Tasting Room — The Rockstar

Cottonwood Main Street. Bold, complex, artistic wines; try Chupacabra and Shinola. Sleek and modern with a full menu next door. Owned by Maynard James Keenan of Tool.

Caduceus Cellars — The Statement

Jerome, on the hillside of the ghost town. Ambitious, premium wines; try Primer Paso and Nagual. Dramatic setting, gallery-style tasting.

Why Book a Private Wine Tour?

The Obvious Reason

Arizona wine country means winding roads through Oak Creek Canyon, four to eight pours per stop, unfamiliar territory, and a long day. A designated driver is not a convenience; it is essential.

Beyond Safety

  • More wineries: nobody holds back because they are driving
  • Better experience: focus on the wine and the company, not navigation
  • Flexibility: linger at favorites, skip the rest
  • Local knowledge: which rooms are crowded and when to arrive
  • Wine transport: buy what you like; we help load it

Verde Valley Wine FAQs

How many wineries can we visit in a day?
Comfortably three or four with a meal. Five or six is ambitious, and after that you stop appreciating the wine.

What about food?
Some wineries have snacks, a few have full restaurants. Plan a real meal in Cottonwood, Jerome, or Cornville.

Can we buy wine and take it home?
Yes. Most wineries also ship. We help load cases into the vehicle.

Can we drink in the vehicle between wineries?
Yes, for passengers 21 and over. Arizona's open-container law exempts passengers in a vehicle for hire such as a party bus or limousine (A.R.S. § 4-251). BYOB, no underage drinking, and the driver never drinks; read the full explainer.

Do we need reservations?
Recommended on weekends, especially at Page Springs and Alcantara. Weekdays are usually walk-in friendly.

Is it actually good wine?
Yes. Arizona wines win national competitions. They are different from California, so embrace the exploration.
